variations.guide.variations.title: Variations
variations.guide.variations.intro: Variations is where you settle changes to the contract before they turn into disputes. Track a change event from a notice, through a priced request, to an agreed order, with daywork sheets and extension-of-time claims running alongside, all the way to the final account.
variations.guide.variations.lifecycle.title: The change lifecycle
variations.guide.variations.lifecycle.body: A change moves through five record types, shown as tabs: a Notice flags the event, a Request prices its cost and schedule impact, an Order is the agreed instruction, Daywork captures work done on a rates basis, and EoT claims handle time extensions. The detail panel draws a stepper across Notice, Request and Order so you always see where a change sits.
variations.guide.variations.notices.title: Raise a notice
variations.guide.variations.notices.body: Issue a notice the moment a contractual event occurs to protect your position and the clock. Each notice records a recipient and a response-by date, then runs through issued, acknowledged, responded and closed as the other party reacts.
variations.guide.variations.requests.title: Price and approve requests
variations.guide.variations.requests.body: A variation request carries the estimated cost and schedule-day impact for review. Submit it, then approve or reject with decision notes. Once approved, convert it straight into a variation order so the agreed figures flow on without re-keying.
variations.guide.variations.orders.title: Agree orders into the final account
variations.guide.variations.orders.body: A variation order is the agreed instruction carrying its final cost and time impact. Start it, complete it or void it as work proceeds. On agreement the order feeds the contract final account and rolls up into Finance, so nothing settled on site is lost. Completed and voided orders are locked from editing.
variations.guide.variations.daywork_eot.title: Daywork and extension-of-time
variations.guide.variations.daywork_eot.body: Daywork sheets log daily labour, material and equipment for owner sign-off, moving from draft to signed to billed. Extension-of-Time claims record a delay cause, requested versus granted days and whether the critical path is affected, then run through submission to a grant or rejection.
variations.guide.variations.dashboard.title: Watch the running impact
variations.guide.variations.dashboard.body: The KPI strip keeps the live picture in view: open notices, pending requests, active orders, total cost impact, schedule impact in days and open EoT claims. Use search and the status filter inside each tab to pull up exactly the records you need.

validation.guide.validation.title: Validation
validation.guide.validation.intro: Validation checks a Bill of Quantities against the rule sets configured for its project and grades the result. Run it as a first-class step in the Import, Validate, Enrich, Estimate pipeline to catch data-quality and compliance issues before you price or tender.
validation.guide.validation.pick_run.title: Pick a BOQ and run
validation.guide.validation.pick_run.body: The project comes from the switcher in the top bar. Choose one of its Bills of Quantities, then click Run Validation. Each run is saved as a report, so when you come back the page restores your last result instead of starting empty.
validation.guide.validation.rule_sets.title: Rule sets are chosen for you
validation.guide.validation.rule_sets.body: You do not pick rules by hand. The engine derives them from the project region and classification standard: boq_quality applies everywhere, and DIN 276, GAEB, NRM or MasterFormat layer on top. The chips above the Run button show exactly which checks will be applied.
validation.guide.validation.score.title: Read the score and summary
validation.guide.validation.score.body: The ring scores the run from 0 to 100 percent, from Poor to Excellent. The summary next to it counts the rules checked and how many passed, raised warnings or failed as errors, so you see the health of the estimate at a glance.
validation.guide.validation.findings.title: Work through the findings
validation.guide.validation.findings.body: Every finding lists below the score. Filter by errors, warnings, info or passed, then expand a row for its message and suggested fix. Where a finding points at a BOQ element you can jump straight to that position in the editor and fix it at the source.
validation.guide.validation.raise_ncr.title: Escalate a blocking error
validation.guide.validation.raise_ncr.body: A failing error can be turned into a formal record. Use Raise NCR on the finding to open the non-conformance register with the rule, message and element reference pre-filled, so a genuine defect is tracked rather than lost.
validation.guide.validation.export.title: Export the results
validation.guide.validation.export.body: When the review is done, export the findings to CSV for sharing or a paper trail, or export the priced BOQ to PDF. The CSV mirrors exactly what is on screen so the file always matches the report you reviewed.

validation.validation.empty_description: Choose a BOQ and click \"Run Validation\" to check its data quality.
validation.validation.error_description: Could not run validation. Check that the BOQ has positions and try again.

daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.title: Daily Site Diary
daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.intro: The daily site diary is your contemporaneous record of what happened on site each day: weather, headcount, deliveries, events, photos and surveys. Open one per site day, fill it in as the day runs, then close and sign it so it stands as tamper-evident proof for delay claims and disputes.
daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.concept.title: One diary per site day
daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.concept.body: A diary is a single dated record for one project day, and the date is its identity. A diary moves through a lifecycle from open to closed to signed to archived, and you cannot open one further ahead than tomorrow because a diary is a record of a day that has happened, not a plan.
daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.tabs.title: Calendar, Today and Archive
daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.tabs.body: The Diaries tab is a month calendar: click a day with a diary to open it, or an empty day to start one. The Today tab is the working record for the selected day, and the Archive tab holds the signed, sealed diaries for the project.
daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.log.title: Log weather, workforce and entries
daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.log.body: On the day record, set the labour and equipment headcount and add diary entries such as deliveries, visitors and events. Weather can be fetched automatically from the project location or added by hand, and the headcount you log here flows into the labour roster used by Payroll.
daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.evidence.title: Attach photos and surveys
daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.evidence.body: Upload site photos for the day and attach drone surveys or reality-capture scans to build a visual record. These assets are tied to the diary date and feed the site photo library, so the evidence stays linked to the day it belongs to.
daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.sign.title: Close, sign and seal
daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.sign.body: A readiness chip shows how complete the diary is and what is still missing before you sign. When the day is done, close it and sign it: a signed diary is sealed with a sha256 fingerprint so any later change is traceable. Unlocking a signed diary preserves the original signature so the integrity break is on record.
daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.export.title: Export and claim evidence
daily-diary.guide.daily_diary.export.body: Export any diary to PDF for the record, or build a hash-sealed SCL Protocol evidence bundle across a date range to support a delay claim. Signed diaries also feed schedule progress, so the daily record does more than sit in a file.

tasks.guide.tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.guide.tasks.intro: Tasks is a Kanban board for the lightweight action items, decisions and follow-ups that keep a project moving, separate from the 4D Schedule that plans the build timeline. Capture them with an assignee, due date, priority and checklist, then move them across columns as the work progresses.
tasks.guide.tasks.board.title: The board and its columns
tasks.guide.tasks.board.body: Every task lives in a status column on the board: Draft, Open, In Progress and Completed. Each column header shows a live count of the cards inside it, so you can read the state of the work at a glance.
tasks.guide.tasks.create.title: Creating a task
tasks.guide.tasks.create.body: Click New Task to open the form. Give it a title, then pick a type, set a priority from Low to Urgent, name an assignee and choose a due date. A task can also carry a checklist whose progress shows on the card as a small bar.
tasks.guide.tasks.types.title: Types and categories
tasks.guide.tasks.types.body: Tasks come in five built-in types: Task, Topic, Information, Decision and Personal, each with its own colour and icon. Need something else? Add a custom category with its own colour, and it becomes a filter tab and a type choice on the form.
tasks.guide.tasks.move.title: Moving work along
tasks.guide.tasks.move.body: Drag a card to another column to change its status, or use the dropdown on the card. Only legal transitions are offered so a move is never rejected. Mark a task Complete from its card, and add your own custom columns to model a workflow that fits your team.
tasks.guide.tasks.find.title: Finding what matters
tasks.guide.tasks.find.body: Use the type tabs to focus the board on one kind of task, and the search box to filter by title, description or assignee. Turn on My Tasks to pull together everything assigned to you across every project in one cross-project list.
tasks.guide.tasks.io.title: Import, export and links
tasks.guide.tasks.io.body: Import brings tasks in from an Excel or CSV file using the provided template, and Export sends the current board out to Excel. Tasks also connect to the rest of the platform: raise them from meetings, RFIs or inspections, and pin them to BIM elements so View in BIM jumps to the geometry.

users.guide.users.title: User Management
users.guide.users.intro: This is the admin panel for your team. Invite people, give each one a role, and tune exactly which modules they can reach. Use it whenever someone joins, leaves, or needs different access.
users.guide.users.invite.title: Invite team members
users.guide.users.invite.body: Admins use Invite User to add a person with their name, email, a starting role and an initial password. The password must be at least 12 characters and include a letter and a digit. The new user appears in the list right away and can sign in immediately.
users.guide.users.roles.title: Roles and what they grant
users.guide.users.roles.body: Every user holds one of four roles: Admin for full access, Manager for project management, Editor to create and edit, and Viewer for read-only. Change a role from the dropdown in the role column. Lowering a role asks you to confirm first, since the person loses the higher access at once.
users.guide.users.access.title: Per-user module access
users.guide.users.access.body: Click Access on any row to open the module matrix. For each module you set whether it is visible and an access level of none, view, edit or full. Presets like All, Viewer and Minimal set everything in one click, and a custom role name labels the mix you build.
users.guide.users.find.title: Find and filter people
users.guide.users.find.body: The stat cards across the top show totals for all users, active accounts, admins and managers. Search by name or email, and use the All, Active and Inactive filter to focus the table on the people you need.
users.guide.users.lifecycle.title: Activate and deactivate
users.guide.users.lifecycle.body: Deactivate revokes a person access at once while keeping their record, so you can reactivate them later if they return. You cannot change your own role or deactivate your own account, which prevents an accidental lockout.
users.guide.users.governance.title: Governance and the audit log
users.guide.users.governance.body: Roles set here decide what each person sees and can do across the platform. For the rules and approval steps behind those roles open Governance, and to review who changed what open the Audit Log, both linked from the intro panel.

documents.guide.documents.title: Documents
documents.guide.documents.intro: Documents is the single register for every file on a project: drawings, contracts, specifications, photos and correspondence. Upload files here, keep their versions and status in order, then hand them off to the people who need them.
documents.guide.documents.upload.title: Upload your files
documents.guide.documents.upload.body: Drag and drop files onto the drop zone, or use Browse Files and Upload Files to pick them. Any file type is accepted, including PDF, images, Excel, DWG and IFC. Each upload is added to a background queue so you can keep working while it finishes.
documents.guide.documents.categories.title: Categories and metadata
documents.guide.documents.categories.body: Every document is filed under a category such as drawing, contract, specification, photo or correspondence. Open Properties on any file to change its category, add a description and apply tags, which makes large registers easy to scan and search.
documents.guide.documents.find.title: Find what you need
documents.guide.documents.find.body: Search by name to jump straight to a file, then narrow the list with the category pills and the file-type and revision filters. Sort by date, name or size, and use the revision filter to show only the latest version or files that have multiple versions.
documents.guide.documents.versions.title: Versions and CDE status
documents.guide.documents.versions.body: Re-uploading a file under the same name keeps a version history, shown as a version badge on the card. ISO 19650 status flows forward from WIP to Shared to Published to Archived, with optional suitability codes, so everyone can see how mature each document is.
documents.guide.documents.preview.title: Preview and open in context
documents.guide.documents.preview.body: Click a PDF or image to preview it in place, with related documents surfaced by semantic similarity. CAD and BIM files open in their viewer, and a PDF can be sent straight to Measure and Takeoff, so a document becomes the start of real work.
documents.guide.documents.distribute.title: Organize and distribute
documents.guide.documents.distribute.body: The document flow runs from Upload to Organize in the CDE to Distribute. Use the actions menu to rename or download a file, or send it on a formal transmittal so the issue is tracked and recipients are recorded.

dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.title: DWG Takeoff
dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.intro: DWG Takeoff opens 2D DWG drawings so you can measure areas, lengths and counts straight off the plan and feed those quantities into your estimate. Use it when your scope lives in DWG or DXF sheets rather than a 3D model.
dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.upload.title: Upload a drawing
dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.upload.body: Drop a DWG or DXF file onto the upload area or click to browse. The file is converted to viewable entities on your own server, so it never leaves your environment. DWG 2000 to 2025 and DXF R12 to R2025 are supported.
dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.layers.title: Layers and entities
dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.layers.body: Once the drawing is open every entity is grouped by its CAD layer. Use the Layers tab to toggle layers on and off and filter by entity type so you isolate just the walls, slabs or pipework you want to measure. Click any entity to read its type, layer and computed quantity.
dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.scale.title: Set the scale
dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.scale.body: A drawing is just pixels until you tell it the scale. Open the Scale tab and pick a preset ratio such as 1:50 or 1:100, calibrate by clicking two points and entering the real distance between them, or set a per-annotation scale for detail views on the same sheet. Every measurement then reports in real-world units.
dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.measure.title: Measure and annotate
dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.measure.body: Pick a tool from the floating palette to measure an area, a length or a perimeter, or to drop a note directly on the drawing. Snap to endpoints and midpoints keeps your clicks precise, and Undo or Redo steps you back through any mistake. Saved measurements live under the Notes tab.
dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.link_boq.title: Link quantities to the BOQ
dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.link_boq.body: Select an entity or measurement and link it to a Bill of Quantities position, either picking an existing line or creating a new one. The quantity flows straight into your cost estimate, keeping the BOQ tied back to the exact place on the drawing it came from.
dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.review.title: Review, compare and export
dwg-takeoff.guide.dwg_takeoff.review.body: The Summary tab rolls up total entities, area and length so you can sanity-check the takeoff at a glance. Compare two revisions to see what changed with a cost delta, export measurements to CSV, or save the current viewport to PDF for the record.

eac.guide.eac.title: EAC Block Editor
eac.guide.eac.intro: EAC stands for Element, Attribute, Constraint. It is a visual editor where you build model checking and quantity rules by dragging blocks onto a canvas, no code required. Use it to define which elements a rule applies to and what each one must satisfy.
eac.guide.eac.concept.title: What an EAC rule is
eac.guide.eac.concept.body: A rule picks a set of model elements, then tests each one against conditions on its attributes. You assemble it from blocks instead of writing logic by hand. Every rule produces one of four results: an aggregate value such as a quantity, a pass or fail check, a clash, or an issue.
eac.guide.eac.palette.title: The block palette
eac.guide.eac.palette.body: The left palette holds every block grouped into Selectors, Logic, Triplet, Attributes, Constraints, Variables and Templates. Search to find a block fast, then drag it onto the canvas. Templates drop a ready-made starter such as external wall thickness so you do not begin from scratch.
eac.guide.eac.selectors.title: Selectors define the set
eac.guide.eac.selectors.body: Start with a selector to decide which elements the rule targets. Match by IFC class, Revit® category, classification code such as Uniformat or DIN, or by spatial container like level, zone or room. Combine selectors with AND, OR and NOT logic to narrow the set precisely.
eac.guide.eac.triplets.title: Attributes, constraints and variables
eac.guide.eac.triplets.body: A triplet pairs an attribute with a constraint, for example wall thickness greater than or equal to 240 mm. Reference a property directly, through an alias, or by regex pattern, and choose from operators covering equality, ranges, sets, text and unit-aware comparisons. Local variables aggregate matched values with sum, average, count, min or max.
eac.guide.eac.canvas.title: Wiring blocks on the canvas
eac.guide.eac.canvas.body: Drop blocks onto the canvas and connect their slots to wire the rule together. Drag to reposition, select to multi-edit, and use Undo, Redo, copy and paste plus Delete to refine the layout. Fit view recenters everything when the graph grows.
eac.guide.eac.run.title: Save, validate and compile
eac.guide.eac.run.body: When the rule looks right, Save layout to persist your work. Validate checks the rule for errors before you rely on it, and Compile turns the blocks into the executable plan that runs against your models.

settings.guide.settings.title: Settings
settings.guide.settings.intro: Settings is where you set the platform up once for your whole workspace. The page is split into tabs down the left side, and the choices you make here flow into every module for this workspace.
settings.guide.settings.general.title: General: profile, theme and mode
settings.guide.settings.general.body: The General tab holds your profile, where you edit your full name and see your email, role and account status. From here you also pick a light, dark or system color scheme and switch the interface between Simple, with the essential estimation tools, and Advanced, with the full professional toolset.
settings.guide.settings.regional.title: Regional formats
settings.guide.settings.regional.body: The Regional tab sets your language, timezone and number, date and currency formats. These choices control how figures and dates are displayed across every module, so set them to match how your team works.
settings.guide.settings.ai.title: Connect an AI provider
settings.guide.settings.ai.body: The AI tab is where you choose a provider such as Anthropic Claude, OpenAI or a local runtime, and paste the API key that powers estimation and analysis. Your key is encrypted and stored securely. Use Test Connection to confirm it works, and set a model name override if a provider renames or retires a model.
settings.guide.settings.integrations.title: Integrations and converters
settings.guide.settings.integrations.body: The Integrations tab wires up Slack, Teams, Telegram and inbound webhooks so the platform can talk to the tools your team already uses. The Converters tab shows the installed DDC converter versions and their GitHub sources, which handle turning CAD and BIM files into estimable data.
settings.guide.settings.advanced.title: Advanced: backup and setup
settings.guide.settings.advanced.body: The Advanced tab covers backup and restore plus the database setup wizard. The Dashboard tab lets you reorder, show or hide the sections on your personal dashboard, saved to this browser.
settings.guide.settings.account.title: Account security
settings.guide.settings.account.body: The Account tab is where you change your password and sign out of all sessions. The Danger Zone groups sensitive actions, including erasing your personal data, and admins can remove the seeded demo projects from here without affecting their own work.

quantities.guide.quantities.title: Quantity Takeoff
quantities.guide.quantities.intro: Quantity Takeoff is the hub for collecting the measured quantities behind an estimate. Pick the route that fits your source, from a written description, PDF drawings, or CAD and BIM models, and every route feeds the same BOQ.
quantities.guide.quantities.methods.title: Three ways to measure
quantities.guide.quantities.methods.body: The method cards are your starting points. Quick Estimate (AI) turns a written scope into priced lines, PDF Takeoff measures areas and lengths on drawings, and CAD/BIM extracts quantities straight from a model. Choose the one that matches the source material you have.
quantities.guide.quantities.register.title: The measured quantities register
quantities.guide.quantities.register.body: Once a project is active, the Measured quantities panel rolls up everything already captured, both takeoff measurements and BOQ line quantities, grouped by unit, trade, type or source with running totals. Filter it, focus a single drawing, or export the rollup to CSV. It is read-only, so the numbers move as you measure more.
quantities.guide.quantities.ai.title: Quick Estimate from text
quantities.guide.quantities.ai.body: When you only have a written description, open Quick Estimate (AI). It reads your scope text and proposes measured, priced lines with confidence scores, so you can review and confirm rather than type every position by hand.
quantities.guide.quantities.pdf.title: Takeoff from PDF drawings
quantities.guide.quantities.pdf.body: PDF Takeoff opens a drawing on a measurement canvas where you click to measure areas, lengths and counts at the right scale. Uploaded drawings appear under Recent Documents so you can pick up where you left off.
quantities.guide.quantities.converters.title: CAD and BIM converter modules
quantities.guide.quantities.flow.title: Upload, measure, into the BOQ
quantities.guide.quantities.flow.body: Every route follows the same three steps: upload or describe the source, measure or extract the quantities, then send them into the estimate. The measured quantities flow into your Bill of Quantities where rates and totals are applied.
quantities.guide.quantities.manual.title: Or enter quantities by hand
quantities.guide.quantities.manual.body: Sometimes a count is faster typed than measured. Quick Manual Entry opens the BOQ Editor so you can add positions and quantities directly, alongside anything captured from AI, PDF or CAD.

markups.guide.markups.title: Markups
markups.guide.markups.intro: Markups are the drawing comments your team leaves on project documents: clouds, arrows, stamps and measurements placed right on a PDF. Use this module to capture review feedback in one place, assign it to a person and track each note from open to resolved.
markups.guide.markups.tools.title: The markup tools
markups.guide.markups.tools.body: Ten markup types cover most review needs: cloud, arrow, text, rectangle, highlight, distance, area, count, stamp and polygon. Each markup carries a label, optional text and a colour, and lives on a specific document and page so it always points at the right detail.
markups.guide.markups.annotate.title: Annotate on the PDF
markups.guide.markups.annotate.body: Click Annotate to open a document in the inline viewer and draw markups straight onto the page. From any markup you can also Open in document to jump back to its exact spot on the source drawing, so a comment is never disconnected from what it refers to.
markups.guide.markups.review.title: Assign, track and approve
markups.guide.markups.review.body: Give a markup an assignee and move it through active, resolved and archived as the work gets done. Filter by type, status or person to focus a review, and route a markup through an approval workflow when it needs a formal sign-off.
markups.guide.markups.connect.title: Measurements and BOQ links
markups.guide.markups.connect.body: Distance, area and count markups hold a real value and unit. Use as takeoff quantity sends that measurement into PDF Takeoff instead of re-keying it, and a markup linked to a BOQ position opens straight to that line so the comment, the quantity and the cost stay connected.
markups.guide.markups.stamps.title: Stamps and revision compare
markups.guide.markups.stamps.body: Place ready-made stamps such as Approved, Rejected or For Review on a page, or build your own custom stamp with its own text and colour. Open Compare to overlay two revisions of a drawing side by side and see exactly what changed.
markups.guide.markups.export.title: See everything and export
markups.guide.markups.export.body: The All annotations tab pulls markups from every source into one feed, while Hub only shows the ones created here. Switch between list and grid views, and Export sends the full set to CSV for sharing or record keeping.

notifications.guide.notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.guide.notifications.intro: The notification inbox collects every alert the platform raises into one place: finished imports, validation results, safety events, approvals and system messages. Use it to stay on top of what needs your attention and to control which events reach you on which channel.
notifications.guide.notifications.inbox.title: Your inbox
notifications.guide.notifications.inbox.body: The Inbox tab lists every notification newest first, with a colored icon for its category and a count of how many are unread. Unread items are highlighted so you can scan what is new at a glance.
notifications.guide.notifications.read.title: Read, navigate and clear
notifications.guide.notifications.read.body: Click a notification to mark it read and jump straight to the record it points at, such as the import, BOQ or risk that raised it. Use Mark all read to clear the unread badge in one step, or the trash icon on a row to remove a single message.
notifications.guide.notifications.filter.title: Filter and page
notifications.guide.notifications.filter.body: The filter switches the list between all, unread only and read only so you can focus on what is still outstanding. When there is more than a page of history, use the pager at the bottom to move through older items.
notifications.guide.notifications.preferences.title: Channel preferences
notifications.guide.notifications.preferences.body: The Preferences tab is a matrix of event types against channels. For each event you can turn in-app, email and webhook delivery on or off, and pick a digest of realtime, hourly or daily. Changes save automatically as you make them.
notifications.guide.notifications.sources.title: Where alerts come from
notifications.guide.notifications.sources.body: Most notifications are raised automatically as work happens across the platform. Threshold alerts from BI Dashboards and outbound rules from Notification Webhooks both flow through this same inbox, so one place shows everything.

schedule.schedule.preview_workers_set: At least {{count}} workers per position where the bill gives no crew ({{positions}} positions), as you set it.
schedule.guide.schedule.title: 4D Schedule
schedule.guide.schedule.intro: The schedule turns your estimate into a time plan: a Gantt of activities with dependencies, the critical path, and a link to the BIM model for a 4D sequence. Use it to lay out the build timeline and see what drives the finish date.
schedule.guide.schedule.create.title: Pick a project and a schedule
schedule.guide.schedule.create.body: Start by choosing a project from the list, then create a schedule inside it with a name and a start date. A project can hold several schedules, so you can keep separate plans for tender, baseline and as-built side by side.
schedule.guide.schedule.activities.title: Add activities by hand or from a BOQ
schedule.guide.schedule.activities.body: Each activity has a name, a WBS code, start and end dates, and a type of task, milestone or summary. Add them one at a time, or use Generate from BOQ to build the whole activity list straight from your priced positions, with durations estimated from quantities.
schedule.guide.schedule.gantt.title: Read the Gantt timeline
schedule.guide.schedule.gantt.body: The Gantt draws every activity as a bar across the timeline, with milestones as diamonds and a marker for today. Zoom from day to year, drag a bar to reschedule it, and follow the arrows between bars to see finish-to-start and other dependency links.
schedule.guide.schedule.cpm.title: Run the critical path
schedule.guide.schedule.cpm.body: Calculate CPM to find the longest chain of dependent activities that sets the project finish date. Critical activities are flagged with a CP badge and highlighted in red, so you know which slips push the whole plan and which have float to spare.
schedule.guide.schedule.risk.title: Test the plan against risk
schedule.guide.schedule.risk.body: Risk analysis runs a PERT pass over the critical path and reports P50, P80 and P95 durations alongside a suggested buffer. Carry that buffer forward into the Risk Register or turn it into cost contingency in the 5D view.
schedule.guide.schedule.progress.title: Track progress and the 4D link
schedule.guide.schedule.progress.body: Drag the slider on any activity to set its percent complete, and the bar fills to match. Link activities to BIM elements so the timeline drives a 4D sequence on the model, and jump back to the source positions in the BOQ at any time.
schedule.schedule.strike_ready_tooltip: Sensor Orçamento {{strength}} of {{target}} MPa ({{pct}}% confidence). Start the strike today?
schedule.schedule.confirm_clear_all: Delete all {{count}} activities of this Cronograma and the links between them? The Cronograma itself stays, and you can generate it again from a Planilha orçamentária. This cannot be undone.

schedule.schedule.delay.checks_title: Check before you rely on this result

schedule.schedule.delay.indicative_note: Indicative result from the Cronograma data, not an expert opinion.

cost-control.cost_control.method_maximum_help: Each line takes its highest figure: budget, Orçamento, award, measured or invoiced. Careful by design: a risk is never hidden behind a lower number.
cost-control.cost_control.method_evm_cpi_help: If half the work is done and it cost 10% more than planned, the rest will likely cost 10% more too. Needs measured work and invoices on the line.
cost-control.cost_control.method_manual_help: You type the expected final cost of a line yourself, with a reason and the document behind it.
cost-control.cost_control.method_best_available_help: Each line takes its most reliable figure: the final account, else the measured work, else the award plus changes, else the Orçamento, else the budget.
cost-control.cost_control.method_maximum_when: Use it when the client wants the cautious figure, or while claims are open.
cost-control.cost_control.method_evm_cpi_when: Use it once work is well under way and progress is measured regularly.
cost-control.cost_control.method_manual_when: Use it on a line where you know more than the data, for example a new offer.
cost-control.cost_control.method_best_available_when: The usual choice. It follows the project as it matures, with nothing to type in.
cost-control.cost_control.source_invoiced_why: The invoices on this line are the highest figure it has, so the maximum method takes them.
cost-control.cost_control.source_evm_why: The cost at completion is projected from progress: what was spent so far, divided by the share of the work done.
cost-control.cost_control.row_loose_changes: Approved changes not on a contract
cost-control.cost_control.ladder_none: No line moved between the two.
cost-control.cost_control.compare_all_lines: Show lines that did not move too
cost-control.cost_control.compare_none: No line moved across these snapshots.
cost-control.cost_control.compare_empty: Freeze a first snapshot, then every later one is compared with it here, line by line.
cost-control.cost_control.method_findings_none: Every forecast is explained: nothing below what is owed, no undocumented move.
cost-control.cost_control.method_save_failed: Could not save the forecast method
cost-control.cost_control.threshold_both: A line that moved by more than {{amount}} and more than {{pct}}% since the last frozen snapshot needs a comment and evidence before the next one can be frozen.
cost-control.cost_control.threshold_amount_only: A line that moved by more than {{amount}} since the last frozen snapshot needs a comment and evidence before the next one can be frozen.
cost-control.cost_control.threshold_pct_only: A line that moved by more than {{pct}}% since the last frozen snapshot needs a comment and evidence before the next one can be frozen.
cost-control.cost_control.threshold_any: Every line that moved since the last frozen snapshot needs a comment and evidence.
cost-control.cost_control.method_subtitle: One method for the whole project. Any line can still be read another way from its drawer.
cost-control.cost_control.threshold_explain: When does a move need a reason? Leave a field empty to skip that test. With both filled in, a move must exceed both.
cost-control.cost_control.threshold_pct: More than (% of the last figure)
cost-control.cost_control.method_fallback: Lines with nothing for their method yet, read by the best available source: {{n}}
cost-control.cost_control.row_allowance: Allowance on the account, not broken down yet
cost-control.cost_control.phases_pct_hint: Each phase against the plan (budget, or the Orçamento where no budget is set).
cost-control.cost_control.phases_hint: Accounts carry the sum of everything below them. Click an account to fold it.
cost-control.cost_control.phases_empty: No cost lines yet, so there is nothing to compare.
cost-control.cost_control.draft_start_subtitle: Takes today's figures into a draft. Write the reason behind each large move, then freeze it: a frozen snapshot is never changed.
cost-control.cost_control.line_method_fallback: The method has nothing to work with on this line yet, so the best available figure stands in.
cost-control.cost_control.line_method_comment_needed: Why this line differs from the project
cost-control.cost_control.line_method_comment_placeho: e.g. claim still open, take the cautious figure
cost-control.cost_control.line_method_manual_note: Your own forecast is in force. Remove it to read the line by a method again.
cost-control.cost_control.draft_delete_confirm: The draft of {{date}} and the reasons written on it are removed for everyone.
cost-control.cost_control.how_5: Choose how the forecast is read: the most reliable figure, the highest one, or projected from progress. Each month start a snapshot, write the reason behind every large move, then freeze it. Frozen snapshots never change.
cost-control.cost_control.note_comment_placeholder: e.g. second offer after the clarification round is 6% higher
cost-control.cost_control.note_needs_both: A comment and at least one piece of evidence are needed.
cost-control.cost_control.draft_explain: This draft is still open. Lines that moved above the threshold need a reason before it can be frozen. Once frozen it is a record and cannot be changed.
cost-control.cost_control.draft_baseline: This is the first snapshot of the project, the baseline every later one is compared with. Nothing needs a reason yet.
cost-control.cost_control.frozen_explain: Frozen on {{date}}. A frozen snapshot is a record and cannot be changed or deleted.
cost-control.cost_control.draft_missing: Lines still waiting for a reason: {{n}}
cost-control.cost_control.snapshot_nothing_moved: No line moved since the last frozen snapshot.
cost-control.cost_control.group_no_account_suspense: No account (suspense): cost lines not yet on the cost structure
cost-control.guide.cost_control.title: Cost control
cost-control.guide.cost_control.intro: Cost control answers one question: what will the project cost in the end, and why. It reads the budget, the estimate, contracts, changes, measured work and invoices that already live in their own modules, so nothing is typed in twice.
cost-control.guide.cost_control.methods.title: Four ways to read the forecast
cost-control.guide.cost_control.methods.body: Best available source takes the most reliable figure of each line and is the usual choice. Maximum value takes the highest figure, for a cautious report. Projected from progress takes what was spent and how much is done, and extends it to the end. Manual is your own figure with a reason. The project has one method; any line can be read another way from its drawer, with a comment.
cost-control.guide.cost_control.snapshots.title: A snapshot every month
cost-control.guide.cost_control.snapshots.body: Start a snapshot and it opens as a draft. Every line that moved by more than the project threshold since the last frozen snapshot asks for a comment and a piece of evidence, a document or meeting minutes. When nothing is missing, freeze it. A frozen snapshot is a record: nobody can change or delete it.
cost-control.guide.cost_control.compare.title: How the cost moved
cost-control.guide.cost_control.compare.body: Step by step walks from one total to the next, the largest move first, with its cause and the reason written for it. Side by side shows several snapshots in columns. The phase comparison shows budget, estimate, best tender, award, changes, measured, invoiced and forecast next to each other on the account tree.
cost-control.guide.cost_control.checks.title: Checks that keep the forecast honest
cost-control.guide.cost_control.checks.body: A forecast below what is already owed needs a document or a comment. A large move on the draft needs its reason. A line on a different method than the project needs a comment. The checks are listed under the forecast method and each one opens its line.
cost-control.guide.cost_control.export.title: Documents for the meeting
cost-control.guide.cost_control.export.body: Export the cost report, the phase comparison, the invoice ledger and the forecast documentation as PDF or Excel, in your language.

onboarding.onboarding.summary_team_hint: Add colleagues and choose their roles
onboarding.onboarding.finish_workspace: The sidebar opens on your {{name}} workspace. Every other screen is one click away under More modules.
onboarding.onboarding.look_subtitle: Pick a style and a menu. The preview shows the result before anything is applied. This step is optional.
onboarding.onboarding.look_later: You can change everything later in Settings > Appearance and Settings > Menu look.
onboarding.onboarding.look_admin_note: As an administrator, Apply also makes this the default for your workspace.
onboarding.onboarding.brand_section_hint: Shown at the top of the menu and on the sign-in page for everyone in this workspace. Optional.

inspections.guide.inspections.title: Inspections
inspections.guide.inspections.intro: Inspections is where site quality is checked and recorded. Schedule a check against a project, verify a checklist on site, record the result, and turn any failure into a tracked Punch List item or a formal NCR so nothing slips through.
inspections.guide.inspections.schedule.title: Schedule an inspection
inspections.guide.inspections.schedule.body: Click New Inspection and give it a title, a type such as structural, electrical, plumbing, fire safety, concrete, waterproofing or handover, a planned date, an inspector and a location. Every inspection belongs to the project you currently have open.
inspections.guide.inspections.checklist.title: Build the checklist
inspections.guide.inspections.checklist.body: Add the items to verify on site and flag the important ones as critical hold points. The checklist describes what to confirm before the work is accepted, and failed items later pre-fill any Punch List item or NCR you raise.
inspections.guide.inspections.lifecycle.title: Start and record the result
inspections.guide.inspections.lifecycle.body: An inspection moves from scheduled to in-progress to completed. Use Start when the inspector goes to site, then Record Result to log the outcome as pass, partial or fail. Completed and failed inspections are locked from further editing.
inspections.guide.inspections.register.title: Track the register
inspections.guide.inspections.register.body: The list shows every inspection with its type, inspector, date, result and status. Counts of total, scheduled, passed and failed sit at the top, and you can search by title, number or inspector and filter by status or type. Expand any row to see its checklist, notes and actions.
inspections.guide.inspections.followup.title: Raise punch items and NCRs
inspections.guide.inspections.followup.body: A fail or partial result unlocks two follow-ups: create a Punch List item for a minor snag to fix and re-check, or raise a formal NCR for a non-conformance needing root-cause analysis and signoff. Both are pre-filled from the inspection and deep-link straight to the new record.
inspections.guide.inspections.export.title: Export the log
inspections.guide.inspections.export.body: Use Export Excel to download the full inspection log for the project, ready for records and client reporting. The same control points tie back to the QMS overview so the inspect, defect and close-out loop stays traceable across the quality cluster.

fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.title: Field Reports
fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.intro: Field reports are the structured daily record of life on site: weather, workforce, work performed, delays and safety. Capture one per day or per event, then take it from draft to approved so it becomes a defensible record you can export and roll up.
fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.types.title: Pick a report type
fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.types.body: Every report has a date and a type: daily, inspection, safety or concrete pour. The type frames what you log, and you can attach a saved template to add the extra fields a given report needs.
fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.weather.title: Log weather and conditions
fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.weather.body: Record the weather condition, temperature, wind, precipitation and humidity for the day. Fill it by hand, or use the location button to pull live weather from your current position when the server has it configured.
fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.workforce.title: Record workforce and work done
fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.workforce.body: Add a line per trade with the number of workers and hours, then note the work performed, delays and delay hours, safety incidents, visitors, deliveries, equipment on site and materials used. The workforce lines total automatically and feed payroll and progress.
fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.workflow.title: Draft, submit, approve
fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.workflow.body: A new report starts as a draft you can keep editing. Submit it for review when it is ready, then approve it with a signature. Approval locks the report permanently, so it can no longer be edited.
fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.views.title: Calendar and list views
fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.views.body: Switch between a month calendar, where each day shows colour-coded status dots, and a filterable list by status and type. Click any day to open its report or start a new one for that date, and watch the summary cards tally totals and workforce hours.
fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.exchange.title: Templates, import and export
fieldreports.guide.fieldreports.exchange.body: Manage reusable templates to standardise what each report captures. Import reports in bulk from Excel or CSV using the download template, export the whole set to Excel, or download any single report as a PDF.

assemblies.assemblies.library.no_single_total: No single total: this preview covers more than one currency, and part of it could not be converted.

resources.guide.resources.title: Resources & Crews
resources.guide.resources.intro: This is where you register the people, crews and equipment that do the work, then put them to work on projects. A request creates demand, an assignment reserves a resource for a date range, and double-booking conflicts are flagged for you so two jobs never claim the same crew.
resources.guide.resources.catalog.title: Your resource pool
resources.guide.resources.catalog.body: The Resources tab is your roster of every person, crew, piece of equipment and subcontractor. Each one has a code, a type, a status of active, on leave or inactive, and a default cost rate. Use New Resource to add one, click the rate to edit it inline, and select rows to export them to CSV.
resources.guide.resources.find.title: Find and sort the roster
resources.guide.resources.find.body: Search by code, name or notes, then narrow the list with the type, status and currency filters. Click any column header to sort, and click a row to open its full detail drawer with skills, certifications and availability.
resources.guide.resources.requests.title: Requests capture demand
resources.guide.resources.requests.body: The Requests tab is the demand side. A foreman or project manager raises a request such as two carpenters with formwork experience next week, with a quantity, priority and date window. Requests are scoped per project, so pick the project first, then track them as open, fulfilled or cancelled.
resources.guide.resources.fulfill.title: Fulfil into an assignment
resources.guide.resources.fulfill.body: A dispatcher fulfils an open request by matching an available resource, which creates an assignment that reserves that resource for the requested dates. You can also propose an assignment directly from the Assignments tab when there is no formal request.
resources.guide.resources.assignments.title: Assignments and conflicts
resources.guide.resources.assignments.body: The Assignments tab is the board of who is reserved and when, moving through proposed, confirmed, in progress and completed. The system flags double-booking conflicts automatically, so you can confirm, cancel or reassign before anyone is committed to two places at once.
resources.guide.resources.portfolio.title: See the bigger picture
resources.guide.resources.portfolio.body: Confirmed assignments are the source of truth for who is on site each day. Jump to Portfolio capacity and Resource leveling to balance workload across projects, and follow the links into the schedule and tasks to keep everything aligned.

meetings.guide.meetings.title: Meetings
meetings.guide.meetings.intro: Meetings is where you schedule, run and document every project meeting so decisions and follow-ups never get lost. Use it for progress reviews, design coordination, safety talks, kickoffs and closeouts, then turn the discussion into tracked action items with an owner and a due date.
meetings.guide.meetings.create.title: Schedule a meeting
meetings.guide.meetings.create.body: Click New Meeting to pick a type, set the date, time and location, and write the agenda or minutes. Each meeting is numbered and sits under the current project, so the full history stays in one place.
meetings.guide.meetings.people.title: Chair and attendees
meetings.guide.meetings.people.body: Set a chairperson and add attendees by picking real people from your contacts, with a free-text fallback for guests who are not in the directory. Linked attendees keep a path back to their record, and you can mark each one present, absent or excused on the day.
meetings.guide.meetings.series.title: Recurring series
meetings.guide.meetings.series.body: For standing site or coordination meetings, use Create recurring series to generate the whole run at once on a weekly or other cadence. Every occurrence lands in the list ready to be filled in as it happens.
meetings.guide.meetings.import.title: Import a transcript
meetings.guide.meetings.import.body: Already held the meeting elsewhere? Use Import Summary to upload a transcript from Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Zoom or Webex. AI extracts the title, key topics, attendees and action items into a preview you review and edit before it is saved.
meetings.guide.meetings.actions.title: Action items flow into Tasks
meetings.guide.meetings.actions.body: Action items captured in a meeting become tracked tasks with an owner and a due date, so follow-ups are visible in the Tasks module and nothing slips. Attach files such as minutes or drawings to keep the supporting documents with the record.
meetings.guide.meetings.track.title: Find, complete and export
meetings.guide.meetings.track.body: The header shows live counts for total, scheduled, in progress and completed meetings. Search by title, number or chair, filter by type and status, mark a meeting complete, and export the minutes to PDF to share.

reporting.guide.reporting.title: Reporting Dashboards
reporting.guide.reporting.intro: Reporting Dashboards turn live project data into role-based KPI views, one project at a time. Use it to check the health of a project at a glance: cost and schedule performance, budget, open items, safety and finance.
reporting.guide.reporting.roles.title: One dashboard per role
reporting.guide.reporting.roles.body: The tabs across the top each frame the same project for a different audience: Executive for the portfolio, Project Manager for delivery, Estimator for cost, Site Engineer for safety and schedule, and Finance for the money. Switch tabs to see the metrics that matter to that role.
reporting.guide.reporting.executive.title: The Executive view
reporting.guide.reporting.executive.body: Executive needs no project selected. It lists every project with its status and KPI traffic lights, plus portfolio totals such as active projects and value grouped by currency. Click any row to make that project active and jump straight to its Project Manager dashboard.
reporting.guide.reporting.kpis.title: Live KPIs and traffic lights
reporting.guide.reporting.kpis.body: Each project is scored on cost (CPI), schedule (SPI), budget consumed and schedule progress, shown as green, amber or red. A dash is not an error: it simply means the project has no cost snapshot yet, so those figures are not measured.
reporting.guide.reporting.project_tabs.title: Project-scoped tabs
reporting.guide.reporting.project_tabs.body: The Project Manager, Estimator, Site Engineer and Finance tabs each need an active project. They pull live stats for that project, open RFIs and overdue tasks, BOQ totals, safety incidents, finance budget and overdue amounts. If none is selected, pick one from the inline project picker.
reporting.guide.reporting.reports.title: Report templates and documents
reporting.guide.reporting.reports.body: The Reports tab lists the report templates and the documents already generated for the active project. Use it to see what is available and what has been produced. For downloadable PDF and Excel files across the workspace, head to the Reports area.
reporting.guide.reporting.refresh.title: Recalculate and where to go next
reporting.guide.reporting.refresh.body: Managers can use Recalculate KPIs to queue a fresh snapshot for every project; the dashboard updates as the figures land. This module covers one project at a time, so for numbers that span every project use Analytics instead.

bim.guide.model_review.title: Model Review
bim.guide.model_review.intro: Model Review is where a coordination meeting happens against the model itself: open the model, walk the open issues one by one with the camera following each, settle them in place, and leave with a record the other side can open in their own tool.
bim.guide.model_review.what.title: What a model review is
bim.guide.model_review.what.body: A review is the meeting and the record around a model. Issues are BCF topics: a title, a status, an owner, a due date, and a saved viewpoint that pins the camera and the elements the issue is about. The Issues page is the project-wide register of those topics; this page is where you work through them with the model in front of you.
bim.guide.model_review.model.title: Pick the model under review
bim.guide.model_review.model.body: Choose a model in the header. Models are converted in the BIM Hub, so if the list is empty, load one there first. The header then shows how many issues are open, how many are late, and how many belong to this model.
bim.guide.model_review.checks.title: Run the automated checks first
bim.guide.model_review.checks.body: Checks on the left run the rule engine over every element and score the model. Each finding can be shown in the 3D view and turned into a tracked issue with one click, so the meeting starts from evidence rather than opinion.
bim.guide.model_review.filter.title: Narrow to what this meeting is about
bim.guide.model_review.filter.body: Use the chips in the Issues dock to keep only what is open, late, unassigned, or raised against the model on screen, then search or filter by discipline, status, priority and assignee. The discipline list is built from the labels this project has actually used, so it also carries whatever else the team labels issues with, including the type and severity the clash check writes. Whatever you leave visible is what the guided walk and the hand-over will cover.
bim.guide.model_review.walk.title: Walk the issues, settle them in place
bim.guide.model_review.walk.body: Start review takes the visible issues one at a time and flies the camera to each saved viewpoint - the arrow keys page through them. Change the status, set an owner and a due date, and drop a note without leaving the model. Clicking any issue in the list does the same thing at your own pace.
bim.guide.model_review.raise.title: Raise an issue from what you see
bim.guide.model_review.raise.body: Select an element, then Raise issue here. The new issue records the camera, the selection and a snapshot of exactly what is on screen, so whoever picks it up lands on the same view you were looking at.
bim.guide.model_review.handover.title: Leave with a record
bim.guide.model_review.handover.body: Finish review closes the meeting with a summary of what was agreed: printable minutes for the file, and a .bcfzip of exactly the issues you walked. BCF is an open exchange format, so the other side opens it in whichever tool they use.

changeorders.guide.changeorders.title: Change Orders
changeorders.guide.changeorders.intro: A change order records a change to the agreed scope along with its cost and schedule impact. Use it whenever work is added, removed or modified after the estimate is set, so every variation is priced and approved before it is committed.
changeorders.guide.changeorders.concept.title: What a change order is
changeorders.guide.changeorders.concept.body: Each order groups one scope change under a code, a title and a reason such as client request, design change or unforeseen conditions. It carries line items, a computed cost impact and a schedule impact in days, giving you a single auditable record of what changed and why.
changeorders.guide.changeorders.create.title: Create an order
changeorders.guide.changeorders.create.body: Click New Change Order to capture the title, description, reason and schedule impact by hand, and optionally apply it to a live contract. Or use AI Draft to generate a starting order from a short prompt, then review and adjust it before submitting.
changeorders.guide.changeorders.items.title: Add line items
changeorders.guide.changeorders.items.body: Each item records the original versus new quantity and rate, and the cost delta is calculated for you. Use Pick from BOQ to seed an item straight from an estimate position so its original values come from the work being amended rather than being re-keyed.
changeorders.guide.changeorders.workflow.title: Move through the workflow
changeorders.guide.changeorders.workflow.body: An order runs Draft, Submitted, Approved and Executed, with rejection available along the way. Open an order to submit it, and route approval either directly or through a named approval chain where each approver signs off in turn before the next step becomes active.
changeorders.guide.changeorders.impact.title: See the impact
changeorders.guide.changeorders.impact.body: The summary cards roll up total orders, approved cost impact, schedule days and pending count for the active project. An approved order is applied to the project budget as a revised commitment, and when it is linked to a contract the contract value is revised on approval too.
changeorders.guide.changeorders.track.title: Track and export
changeorders.guide.changeorders.track.body: The table lists every order with its code, status, reason, cost impact and dates. Filter by status to focus on what is in flight, and use Export CSV to hand the full list to finance or reporting.
changeorders.changeorders.approver_user_ids_hint: Steps run sequentially: step 1 acts first, then step 2, etc. Each approver only sees the Alteração de contrato when their step becomes active.

reports.guide.reports.title: Reports
reports.guide.reports.intro: Reports turns the live data in a project into a finished document you can hand over: a detailed BOQ, a cost breakdown, a GAEB tender file, validation results, a schedule summary and more. Use it when a client, authority or subcontractor needs a deliverable instead of a screenshot.
reports.guide.reports.concept.title: What this module produces
reports.guide.reports.concept.body: Each card on this page generates one report and downloads it as a file in the format your recipient expects: PDF, Excel, CSV, GAEB XML, HTML or plain text. The numbers are pulled straight from the BOQ, cost model, schedule and risk data, so what you send always matches what is on screen.
reports.guide.reports.select.title: Pick a project and BOQ first
reports.guide.reports.select.body: Choose the project from the selector in the top bar, then pick a BOQ from the dropdown on this page. BOQ-based reports such as the detailed BOQ and the GAEB export need a BOQ selected, while project-wide reports like cost, schedule and risk only need the project.
reports.guide.reports.generate.title: Generate a report
reports.guide.reports.generate.body: Click the format button on any card to build and download that report on the spot. The detailed BOQ exports to PDF or Excel, GAEB X83 is for tender exchange, and the cost, validation, schedule, 5D, tender comparison, change order, risk, cash flow and progress reports each download with one click.
reports.guide.reports.builder.title: Custom report builder
reports.guide.reports.builder.body: Open Configure Sections to assemble one combined HTML report from the parts you want: executive summary, budget vs actual, cost breakdown, BOQ detail, earned value, schedule and risk. Tick the sections you need and generate a single document tailored to the audience.
reports.guide.reports.history.title: Recently generated reports
reports.guide.reports.history.body: The history list at the bottom shows reports that were generated and stored for the selected project, so you can find and re-download an earlier deliverable without rebuilding it from scratch.
reports.guide.reports.share.title: Hand it over
reports.guide.reports.share.body: Every report downloads as a self-contained file you can attach to an email, upload to a portal or print. GAEB XML goes back into another estimating tool, Excel and CSV open in any spreadsheet, and the HTML and PDF reports are ready to read as they are.

match-elements.match_wizard.step1_help: Pinning a phase narrows BIM elements and catalogue rates to that work. Pick \"Any stage\" to search across the whole project.

Rates are sourced from the regional book; switch if you want rates from elsewhere.
match-elements.match_wizard.step3_help: BIM gives quantity-aware matches. Excel and pasted text are good for ad-hoc lists.

punchlist.guide.punchlist.title: Punch List
punchlist.guide.punchlist.intro: The Punch List is the running register of snags and minor defects that have to be fixed before handover. Use it near the end of a job to capture outstanding work, assign an owner and a deadline, and drive every item through to a verified close-out.
punchlist.guide.punchlist.capture.title: Capture a snag
punchlist.guide.punchlist.capture.body: Click New Item to log a snag with a title, description, priority from low to critical, a category such as structural or finishing, and a location. Assign it to a team member and set a due date so every item has an owner and a deadline. You can also pin it to a drawing sheet so the issue can be reopened on the plan.
punchlist.guide.punchlist.lifecycle.title: The status lifecycle
punchlist.guide.punchlist.lifecycle.body: Each item moves Open to In Progress to Resolved to Verified to Closed. The owner works it up to Resolved, then a checker verifies the fix and closes it. If a fix does not hold up on a re-check, reopen the item straight back to Open from Resolved, Verified or Closed. The backend enforces the flow, so only legal moves are offered.
punchlist.guide.punchlist.views.title: List and Kanban views
punchlist.guide.punchlist.views.body: Switch between a Kanban board to manage flow across the status columns and a list view for bulk triage and close-out. Search by title, description or location, and use the filters to narrow by priority, status, category or assignee. Overdue items are flagged in red so nothing slips.
punchlist.guide.punchlist.kpis.title: Read the KPI strip
punchlist.guide.punchlist.kpis.body: The KPI band at the top tracks the live workload: open items, overdue, critical and high priority, resolved and awaiting verify, closed this week, and the average days to close. Click a tile to filter the list below to that slice, so you can jump straight to the work that needs attention.
punchlist.guide.punchlist.sources.title: Items from other modules
punchlist.guide.punchlist.sources.body: Punch items can be raised automatically from a failed inspection, an NCR or a model clash. These carry a source badge you can click to open the record they came from, which keeps the inspect, defect and close-out loop traceable right through to handover.
punchlist.guide.punchlist.close_out.title: Bulk close and map
punchlist.guide.punchlist.close_out.body: When a zone is signed off, multi-select items in the list view and bulk close the batch in one step. Each item holds its own photos for evidence, and View on map plots snags by location so you can see what is outstanding across the site.

dashboard.guide.dashboard.delivery.title: Delivery and quality widgets
dashboard.guide.dashboard.delivery.body: Five widgets track the delivery and quality work on your active project and each carries a How it works note you can open right on the card. Upcoming Milestones lists the next key schedule dates with days remaining or overdue. RFI Turnaround shows open and overdue requests for information and the average days to a response. Submittals splits pending review, approved and overdue. Inspections gives the pass rate with open and failed counts. Punch List shows open and overdue items with the average days to close. Each card stays hidden until its module has data, so a new project starts clean and the cards appear as you begin using each area.
